minutes.headline: Board awarded $9M school bonds and leaned toward borrowing the rest early in spring 2015
minutes.summary: The board heard the financial advisor on financing the middle/high school project, awarded the bond issue to the low bidder, and discussed borrowing the remainder earlier, asking for projections. It waived school building permit fees and appointed the town manager temporary treasurer/collector. Announcements, a proclamation and committee reports filled the rest.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to award the school general obligation bond issue as detailed in the form of the vote.
The board asked for projections comparing larger earlier borrowing with later options, and their tax impact, to be checked with the school building committee before choosing a spring approach.
The board voted to waive building permit fees for the middle/high school project only; plumbing and electrical fees were not waived.
The board appointed the town manager temporary treasurer/collector from November 14 until a successor is appointed; a recommendation is expected December 2.
The next meeting is November 18, since November 11 is Veterans Day.

why_it_matters: How the remaining school project debt is borrowed, in one larger issue or in notes later refunded by bonds, shifts when the cost reaches the tax rate and adds interest over the life of the bonds.

The permit fee waiver means the town does not collect those building fees on the school project, and the treasurer/collector post, which handles tax bills and payments, is covered by the town manager for now.
watch_next: December 2: a recommendation on the permanent treasurer/collector is expected.
The board's projections on earlier borrowing and its tax impact, ahead of the spring 2015 borrowing decision.
